newsitem.title: INDONESIA: E.Timorese meet U.N. envoy after embassy protest.
newsitem.headline: E.Timorese meet U.N. envoy after embassy protest.

text.p: A group of East Timorese youths secured a meeting with a U.N. special envoy on Tuesday after breaking into the Austrian Embassy in Jakarta and staging a demonstration for self-determination in their homeland.
Three of the youths were taken to meet Jamsheed Marker, the special envoy for East Timor currently on a visit to Indonesia, at the United Nations headquarters in Jakarta.

"We have met him and we told him of our aspirations," said Mariano Sabino Lopez, a spokesman for the group. "We do not mean to create hostility against the Indonesian government but (want) a way to open more dialogure on East Timor."
He said the delegation demanded the release of all political prisoners in East Timor, the freeing of East Timorese independence leader Xanana Gusmao and a referendum on the future of the territory.

Journalists and police crowded around the gate of the Austrian Embassy, located in a residential suburb of Jakarta, after thirty-three East Timorese entered the mission compound around 1 p.m. (0600 GMT).

Unfurling banners, including one saying "Viva Timor Leste" (Long Live East Timor), they scaled the embassy gate and asked embassy officials to set up a meeting with Marker, who returned to Jakarta on Monday after a three-day visit to East Timor.
"We are here, 33 of us, inside the embassy. We want the embassy to become a mediator for us to meet the U.N. envoy," Lopez told Reuters from inside the embassy compound.
"We want to make it clear that we are not seeking asylum. We want to stay here until our demand is met. We may want to stage a hunger strike if necessary," he said.

Some seven hours later, the group was still inside the mission, although the three who met Marker had returned. It was not immediately known what their plans were, although Lopez said they intended to leave the embassy once their aims had been accomplished.
Ambassador Hans Demel said the group would stay in the embassy overnight.
Since September 1995, 108 East Timorese have entered foreign embassies in Jakarta and asked for asylum. They have been granted asylum in Portugal, the former colonial ruler of East Timor.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
